generated_by: VFM Studio DIC data agent (deterministic analysis; numbers are measured, not estimated by the language model)

format_check.expected: raw Vic-3D facet export: one row per facet with the 33 columns X, Y, Z, U, V, W, exx, eyy, exy, e1, e2, gamma, cxx, cyy, cxy, c1, c2, gamma_c, sigma, x, y, u, v, q, r, q_ref, r_ref, SIGMA_X, SIGMA_Y, SIGMA_Z, Xp, Yp, Zp
format_check.cross_file_checks: same facet step in every file of a test; every file shares at least half its facets with the first

conventions.increments: Δ quantities are relative to step 1 of each test, in the order the user confirmed
conventions.axes: figures and zone names use +X to the right and +Y up

noise_model.equation: σ_c(x) = σ_int,c · s_c(x),  s_c = 1 + (g_c − 1)/c,  g_c = ‖w_c(x)‖/‖w_c(full)‖ (Vic-3D 15×15 local quadratic stencil, truncated at every boundary of the facet mask)
calibrated_on: 45_deg Laminate A1_PB, A1_Twist, A2_PB, A2_Twist, B1_PB, B1_Twist, B2_PB, B2_Twist
known_limits: calibrated on 45° laminate coupons; other laminates, speckle patterns or camera set-ups are extrapolations
measured interior levels differ by about 2× between specimens in the calibration set
fitted on plain coupons alone c = 1.244, on cutouts alone 1.582
noise_model.curvature_convention: κ = (−2·cxx, −2·cyy, +2·cxy); κxy is the engineering twist

solver_data.layout: Layout A (nodes) — one .mat per load step, read by vfm_data_io
solver_data.conversion: Vic-3D → plate theory: κₓₓ = −2 cxx, κᵧᵧ = −2 cyy, κₓᵧ = +2 cxy (Vic-3D cxx = ½ ∂²w/∂x², cxy = −∂²w/∂x∂y; solver κₓₓ = −∂²w/∂x², κₓᵧ = −2 ∂²w/∂x∂y). Strains: εₓₓ = exx, εᵧᵧ = eyy, γₓᵧ = 2 exy (Vic-3D exy is tensor shear).
solver_data.note: values are absolute per frame, as the Import-steps dialog writes them; the solver works with increments relative to its reference step

deformation.final_step_rule: step with the largest change of the dominant machine moment

w_quadratic_fit_final_step.note: quadratic fit of the final-step ΔW; agreement in sign and size with the mean Δκ checks that the curvature convention and the displacement field tell the same story

curvature_frame_check.verdict: consistent: the Vic curvature tensor matches the ΔW surface as exported
curvature_frame_check.solver_data_note: solver arrays are built with the standard conversion used by the VFM Studio importer; nothing is re-oriented automatically

noise.estimator: pointwise temporal residual: at every facet, each curvature component is regressed on {1, T, T²} across the 11 steps and the residual scatter is taken (8 degrees of freedom per facet), divided by 0.958 (median of sqrt(chi2/dof)) so that medians compare like for like with the calibration, which used 35-frame static stacks. Anything the quadratic in load cannot follow (slip, local damage, re-correlation jumps) also counts as noise, so this is an upper bound on sensor noise.

recorded_in_export.not_in_export: subset size, strain/curvature filter size and weighting, correlation criterion and interpolation are not written to the raw facet export; they are inferred below

subset.method: spatial autocorrelation of the per-facet temporal residual of U, V, W (the same load-polynomial residual the noise estimator uses), high-passed per step by subtracting a local quadratic over 31×31 facets (removes rigid-body jitter and other smooth motion the load polynomial cannot follow). Overlapping subsets share pixels, so their displacement errors correlate roughly in proportion to the shared area; for a uniformly weighted square subset that falls to 0.5 at a separation of half a subset, so subset ≈ 2 × (half-correlation lag) × facet step
subset.estimate_from: median of the U and V half-correlation lags along X and Y
subset.caveat: an estimate, not a recorded setting: subset weighting, interpolation and correlated speckle or lighting changes shift it by about a facet step either way

curvature_filter.method: the final-step ΔW is re-fitted with a local quadratic over every candidate window (5…31 facets; uniform and gaussian weights), truncated at the facet mask, and the resulting Δκ is compared with the exported Δκ on facets whose full window lies inside the mask. mismatch = RMS(refit − exported) / SD(exported); 0 is an exact reproduction, 1 means the refit explains none of the exported scatter
curvature_filter.note: size and weighting trade off along a valley (a wider window with faster decay smooths like a narrower uniform one); the gaussian sigma is better determined than the size

curvature_filter_sweep.definitions: each row re-fits ΔW with that filter size (weighting fixed at the identified one). noise: same temporal-residual estimator as the noise section, on the refitted curvature; interior = facets whose full window lies inside the mask; edge = ≤ 2 facets from a boundary. signal: interior mean Δκ of the dominant component at the final step; snr_interior = |signal| / interior noise. dW_fit_rms_misfit_um: median RMS residual of the local quadratic fit of the final-step ΔW; noise_only_fit_rms_misfit_um: the same fit applied to the temporal-residual W fields (noise alone); misfit_to_noise_ratio = their quotient (its absolute level depends on how the frames share noise, so only its change with size matters); smoothing_bias_index = that ratio divided by its value at the smallest size: 1 means the larger window follows ΔW as well as the smallest, a rise marks smoothing bias (the window is wider than the deformation features). white_noise_sigma_relative_to_identified: noise ratio expected if W noise were uncorrelated between facets

read_quality.zone_layout: 5 bands along Y (bottom→top) × 3 along X (left→right), on the bounding box of the measured region

automatic_checks.observation: κxy signal-to-noise at the final step is 1.35
the noise model's stencil (uniform 15 facets) reproduces the exported curvature with mismatch 0.75, against 0.27 for the inferred filter (15 facets, gaussian, edge weight 5% of centre)
